newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran hints EU envoys can return, Bonn to be last.
newsitem.headline: Iran hints EU envoys can return, Bonn to be last.

text.p: Iran's outgoing President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani has indicated that ambassadors of European Union states may return to Tehran but Bonn's envoy must be the last.
Rafsanjani, who ends his term in office on Monday when President-elect Mohammad Khatami is sworn in, was speaking in interviews on Iranian television and radio on Saturday night.

Asked to comment on indications by EU countries that they were ready to send their envoys back to Iran, Rafsanjani said: "That is true. They are now ready to return since the leader of the revolution (Ayatollah Ali Khamenei) said that they can do so. Germany must return after everyone else."
He said the European states wanted to return together but that Iran would deal with each country separately.

EU states except for Greece recalled their ambassadors from Tehran after a German court concluded in April that Iran's top leaders had ordered the 1992 assassination of four Iranian Kurdish dissidents in a Berlin restaurant.
The EU also suspended all ministerial contacts as well as its policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran.
Iran, which has repeatedly denied involvement in the killings, retaliated by withdrawing its ambassadors from European capitals.
But when the EU countries later decided to send their ambassadors back to the Iranian capital, Khamenei said the German ambassador, Horst Beschmann, was not welcome in Tehran.
The EU in May sent a delegation to Tehran for talks with officials on the strained relations.
"You must sort yourself out. If you wish to work with Iran, you should not resort to such ploys," Rafsanjani said on Saturday night.
"They (European countries) thought that we will retreat in the face of this pressure and make concessions, but they realized that Iran is far stronger than to be frightened by such ploys," he said.
"However, this has not ended yet. The issue can go on, but eventually the Europeans must accept that they have made a mistake," he added.
